newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - September 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - September 16.

text.p: Following are the highlights of stories reported in the Irish press on Monday.
- The IRA is understood to be moving closer to renewing its ceasefire and is preparing to hold a General Army Convention despite denials by republican organisation Sinn Fein.
- The final of the All-Ireland football championship ended in a draw between counties Mayo and Meath in Croke Park in Dublin. The replay will take place in two weeks' time.
- Pro British loyalists heckled and obstructed mass-goers outside Catholic churches in County Antrim on Sunday in a new twist in the inter-communal bitterness.
- Dunnes may have lost up to 2.5 million Irish pounds and valuable market share in its two-week long staff strike which ended last Saturday.
- Serious tensions between the board and management of Irish state health insurance company VHI may surface when it holds a meeting of the company board on Friday.
- The Irish parliament's committee on enterprise and economic strategy is to be asked to hold its own inquiry into the affairs of two investment brokers who left Ireland owing money to clients.
- Leading IRA figures in favour of a new ceasefire have gained majority control of the republican movement, senior Irish police officers said at the weekend.
- A man escaped death when two gunshots were fired into a parked car in Dublin city on Sunday night.
- A young child died and another was in hospital after a pleasure boat with seven passengers sank when it encountered rough waters in Dundalk Bay on Sunday.
- Pilots in Irish national airline Aer Lingus voted on Sunday to go on strike for a 17 percent pay rise.

- Irish state telecommunications company Telecom Eireann has played down weekend reports that its rival Esat Telecom is to ask the European Commission to block Telecom Eireann's proposed alliance with KPN-Telia.

- The Competition Directorate of the EU has ruled that there was no infringement of the rules on State Aid by the UK government which provided aid to the Northern Ireland concrete and quarrying industry between 1980 and 1985.
- German media reported on Sunday that Irish crystal and china company Waterford Wedgewood is planning to take over loss-making German rival, Rosenthal AG.
